evals.prompt: Using the security-and-hardening skill, threat-model a new feature before it's built: users can register a webhook URL that our server will POST order events to. Identify the trust boundary, name at least two STRIDE threats that apply, and state the tier (Always/Ask First/Never) any file-upload-adjacent decision would fall into if we later add attachment support to the webhook payload.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the outbound webhook call as a trust boundary/SSRF risk, names STRIDE categories like spoofing or information disclosure or denial of service, and correctly places adding file uploads in the Ask First tier.

assertions.text: Identifies SSRF risk from the webhook URL
Places file upload handling in the Ask First tier

evals.expected_output: Flags the SSRF risk of fetching a raw user-supplied URL and recommends a host allowlist plus checking that all resolved IPs are public/unicast, rejecting private or link-local addresses including the cloud metadata address.

evals.prompt: Using the security-and-hardening dependency-audit triage guidance, classify how urgently to act: `npm audit` reports a HIGH severity vulnerability in a devDependency used only in the test runner, with no fix currently available.
evals.expected_output: Classifies this as not reachable in production (dev-only), so not an immediate blocker, but recommends tracking it, checking for workarounds, and revisiting when a fix is available or considering a replacement.

assertions.text: Recommends tracking or a workaround rather than ignoring it
